# A Quiet Morning (clean)

Adrian Voss preferred black coffee to tea, as always. He kept rooms at Number
Seven, Grey Lane, and played the violin while Helen Carr — a physician lately
returned from service overseas — wrote in her notebook.

Mrs. Bramley, who is sixty and keeps three cats, left toast outside the door.
The Amber Circle still meets above a bookshop in Harbour Street.

Carr also noted a new detail: Voss has begun cataloguing his chemical bottles
by colour as well as by name.
